newsitem.title: UK: UK's Berkeley to develop Harrods property.
newsitem.headline: UK's Berkeley to develop Harrods property.

text.p: British property company Berkeley Group Plc said on Wednesday it had acquired a 10-acre site near London's River Thames occupied by Harrods Depositor from businessman Mohamed Al Fayed, the owner of Harrods departmental store.
Berkeley said it would convert the site into a complex of 250 residential units offering about 300,000 square feet, in association with Harrods. The development will be called 'Harrods Village'.
Neither Berkeley nor Al Fayed's office would disclose the value of the transaction. Al Fayed's office also declined to say how much royalty will be paid for using the 'Harrods' name.
Berkeley said development of the complex would retain the original Victorian architecture of the main building with the new designs complementing it.
Harrods Depository was originally built in 1892 using materials from the old Piccadily underground railway station.
The company said the development of Harrods Village would commence this summer with a worldwide marketing programme launching in autumn.
